edges.effect_quant: The literature is mostly case-based, but the direction is consistent: chronic nitrofurantoin prophylaxis can produce interstitial lung disease and pulmonary fibrosis, especially in older adults after months to years of exposure. Reported cases include elderly patients developing respiratory failure or oxygen-dependent fibrosis after prolonged prophylaxis, sometimes with radiographic reversal after drug withdrawal and sometimes with incomplete recovery.
edges.population: older adults receiving prolonged nitrofurantoin therapy or prophylaxis for recurrent urinary tract infections
edges.mechanism: Chronic nitrofurantoin lung toxicity likely reflects cumulative oxidative and immune-mediated injury to the pulmonary interstitium, leading to organizing pneumonia, chronic interstitial pneumonitis, and eventually fibrosis. Older adults receiving prophylaxis for long periods appear particularly vulnerable because exposure accumulates silently before dyspnea becomes obvious.
edges.summary: Even though this edge rests mostly on case literature rather than large cohorts, the signal is clinically important and plausibly causal. Long-term nitrofurantoin in older adults has repeatedly been linked to interstitial lung disease and fibrotic lung injury, which is why prophylactic use deserves periodic review instead of being treated as benign indefinitely.
edges.caveats: This is not a common toxicity in absolute terms, and the absence of large comparative cohorts means the incidence is uncertain. The right interpretation is therefore a rare but real harm signal that matters because the consequence can be severe, not a claim that most older adults on nitrofurantoin will develop fibrosis.

new_entities.name: Pulmonary fibrosis
